outcomes.stem: Over the last 2 weeks, how often has the client been bothered by the following problems?

items: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Poor appetite or overeating
Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way
Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Trouble relaxing
Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
Feeling afraid, as if something awful might happen

residency.title: Canadian data residency
residency.body: Your records are stored in Supabase (AWS ca-central-1, Montréal). AI Assist, when you turn it on, sends note text to Anthropic in the United States.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication required
mfa.body: Client records can only be read or changed from a session that has passed a TOTP challenge. This is enforced by the database, not just the app.

isolation.title: Only you can see your records
isolation.body: Row-level security scopes every client, note, invoice and appointment to your account — including inside a group practice. MentalPath staff access requires service credentials and is not part of normal operation.

locked.title: Locked notes are permanent
locked.body: Once locked, a note cannot be edited or deleted — corrections are added as dated amendments, as College record-keeping standards expect.

audit.title: Every change and note view is logged
audit.body: The audit log below is written by the database itself. You cannot edit or delete it, and neither can the app.

signout.title: Automatic sign-out
signout.body: You are signed out after 15 minutes of inactivity. Note drafts are never stored in your browser.

encryption.title: Notes encrypted with your own key
encryption.body: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. Session-note content is additionally encrypted in the database with a key unique to your account, so backups and database copies contain only ciphertext.

retention.title: Retention handled for you
retention.body: Records are kept 10 years after the last contact (or 10 years after a client turns 18, whichever is later), then destroyed automatically.

compliance.custodian: You remain the health information custodian for your clients' records. MentalPath acts as your agent/service provider and does not certify your compliance with PHIPA, PIPEDA or your College's standards.

breach.title: If you suspect a privacy breach
breach.contain: Contain it. Change your password, sign out other sessions (Settings → Security), and remove any shared access.
breach.tell: Tell us at privacy@mentalpath.ca if it may involve MentalPath systems. We will notify you without delay if we detect a breach affecting your records.
breach.assess: Assess and notify. As custodian, Ontario's PHIPA (s. 12) requires you to notify affected individuals at the first reasonable opportunity and, in prescribed cases, the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario. Other provinces and PIPEDA have their own rules.
breach.record: Record it. Keep a record of what happened, who was affected and the steps you took. Your College may also need to be informed.
breach.disclaimer: This is general information, not legal advice. Check the current requirements with your College or the IPC.

privacyPage.title: How MentalPath handles your data
privacyPage.updated: Last updated September 25, 2026 · Summary pending legal review

responsible.title: Who is responsible
responsible.body: Clinicians who use MentalPath are the custodians of their clients' health information. MentalPath stores and processes that information on their behalf, only to provide the service.

stored.title: Where data is stored
stored.body: Client records, session notes, outcome measures, appointments and invoices are stored in Canada (Supabase on AWS, Montréal region). Card payments are handled by Stripe; MentalPath never sees full card numbers.

leaves.title: Data that can leave Canada
leaves.ai: AI Note Assist is off by default. If a clinician turns it on, the note text they choose to draft from is sent to Anthropic in the United States. Phone numbers, emails, health card numbers, SINs, postal codes and dated birthdates are removed first.
leaves.telemetry: Error monitoring and product analytics, when enabled, receive technical events only — never client information, note text or page contents.

protected.title: How records are protected
items: Each clinician can only access their own records, enforced by the database — including within a group practice.
Two-factor authentication is required to access client records.
Session-note content is encrypted in the database with a key unique to each clinician; data is also encrypted in transit and at rest by our hosting provider.
Locked notes can't be edited or deleted; corrections are added as dated amendments.
Every change and every note view is recorded in an audit log the clinician can review.

retention.title: Keeping and deleting records
retention.body: Clinicians can download all of their data at any time. When an account is closed, sign-in is blocked immediately, and clinical records are kept for the retention period required by Ontario's regulatory Colleges (10 years after the last contact, or 10 years after the client turns 18, whichever is later) and are then destroyed automatically.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: If you are a client, contact your clinician to access or correct your records. Clinicians and anyone else can reach our privacy contact at <mail>privacy@mentalpath.ca</mail>. You can also contact the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada.
